nodes.summary: Every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that is contained in a finite union of almost thin sets is contained in a finite union of Sidon sets; that is, the ideal generated by the almost thin sets is contained in the Sidon ideal.
nodes.title: The almost thin ideal is contained in the Sidon ideal

nodes.summary: For a set $Z \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, let $D(Z) = \{a - b : a, b \in Z,\ b < a\}$ be its set of positive differences. The ideal $D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ consists of the sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ for which there is a natural number $n$ such that $D(Z) \not\subseteq A$ for every $n$-element set $Z \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The ideal of sets avoiding large difference sets

nodes.summary: The empty set belongs to the ideal $D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ of sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ for which some natural number $n$ satisfies $D(Z) \not\subseteq A$ for every $n$-element set $Z \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, where $D(Z)$ is the set of positive differences $a - b$ with $a, b \in Z$ and $b < a$.
nodes.title: The empty set lies in the difference-set ideal

nodes.summary: The empty subset of $\mathbb{N}$ belongs to the van der Waerden ideal.
nodes.title: The empty set lies in the van der Waerden ideal

nodes.summary: There exist a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a real constant $c > 0$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| > c\, (n \log n)^{1/3}$ for every natural number $n \ge 1$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi lower bound for an infinite Sidon set

nodes.summary: There exist a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a real constant $c > 0$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| > c\, n^{1/3}$ for every natural number $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Mian–Chowla lower bound for an infinite Sidon set

nodes.summary: There is a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for every real $\varepsilon > 0$, the inequality $|A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| > n^{\sqrt{2} - 1 - \varepsilon}$ holds for all sufficiently large natural numbers $n$; that is, $|A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| > n^{\sqrt{2} - 1 - o(1)}$.
nodes.title: Ruzsa's lower bound for an infinite Sidon set

nodes.summary: There is a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that is not contained in any finite union of almost thin sets; that is, $A$ does not belong to the ideal generated by the almost thin sets.
nodes.title: A Sidon set outside the almost thin ideal

nodes.summary: There is a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that belongs to the van der Waerden ideal, is contained in a finite union of gap-lacunary sets (infinite sets whose gaps between consecutive elements tend to infinity), and belongs to the ideal $D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ of sets avoiding large difference sets, but is not contained in any finite union of Sidon sets.
nodes.title: A set in the van der Waerden, lacunary and difference-set ideals outside the Sidon ideal

nodes.summary: Every weak Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is the union of two disjoint Sidon sets $B$ and $C$.
nodes.title: Weak Sidon sets split into two Sidon sets

nodes.summary: The ideal on $\mathbb{N}$ generated by the weak Sidon sets equals the Sidon ideal.
nodes.title: Weak Sidon sets generate the Sidon ideal

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a property of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$. If $A$ lies in the ideal generated by $P$ and $B \subseteq A$, then $B$ also lies in the ideal generated by $P$.
nodes.title: Generated ideals are closed under subsets

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a property of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$. The ideal generated by $P$ is the family of all sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that are contained in the union of finitely many sets with property $P$. The empty union is allowed, so the empty set always belongs to it.
nodes.title: Ideal generated by a property

nodes.summary: Every almost thin set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Almost thin sets are infinite

nodes.summary: Every gap-lacunary set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Gap-lacunary sets are infinite

nodes.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is *almost thin* if it is infinite and, writing $A(n)$ for its $n$-th element in increasing order (counting from $n = 0$), there is a real number $\alpha < 1$ such that $A(n)/A(n+1) \le \alpha$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
nodes.title: Almost thin set

nodes.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is *gap-lacunary* (called *lacunary* in the source) if it is infinite and, writing $A(n)$ for its $n$-th element in increasing order (counting from $n = 0$), the gaps $A(n+1) - A(n)$ tend to infinity as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Gap-lacunary set

nodes.summary: Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $0 \notin A$, and write $A(n)$ for the $n$-th element of $A$ in increasing order, counting from $n = 0$, with $A(n) = 0$ when $A$ has at most $n$ elements. If $2 A(n) \le A(n+1)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, then $A$ is a Sidon set.
nodes.title: Positive sets whose elements at least double are Sidon

nodes.summary: Every Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a weak Sidon set.
nodes.title: Sidon sets are weak Sidon sets

nodes.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a *weak Sidon set* (or *well spread*) if sums of two distinct elements of $A$ are distinct: whenever $a, b, c, d \in A$ satisfy $a < b$, $c < d$ and $a + b = c + d$, then $a = c$.
nodes.title: Weak Sidon set

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a property of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$. Every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with property $P$ lies in the ideal generated by $P$, the family of all subsets of finite unions of sets with property $P$.
nodes.title: Sets with a property lie in the ideal it generates

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and $C \ge 1$ be natural numbers, and put $M = C \cdot 2^n + 1$ and $K = (n - 1)\binom{n}{2} + 1$. Then the block $\mathrm{Block}(n, C, M, K) = \{M l + C \cdot 2^k : 0 \le k < n,\ 1 \le l \le K\}$ is not contained in the union of any $n - 1$ Sidon subsets of $\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: A block not covered by few Sidon sets

nodes.summary: For a set $Z \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, the positive difference set $D(Z)$ is the set of all differences $a - b$ with $a, b \in Z$ and $a > b$.
nodes.title: Positive difference set

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $C$ and $M$, the block $\mathrm{Block}(1, C, M, 1) = \{M l + C \cdot 2^k : 0 \le k < 1,\ 1 \le l \le 1\}$ is the singleton $\{M + C\}$.
nodes.title: One-term blocks

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $C$, $M$ and $K$, the block $\mathrm{Block}(n, C, M, K)$ is the set of natural numbers $M l + C \cdot 2^k$ with $0 \le k < n$ and $1 \le l \le K$.
nodes.title: Block sets

nodes.summary: Give the Cantor space $\{0, 1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ the product topology and identify each set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with its indicator function. Then the set of indicator functions of the members of the Sidon ideal is a countable union of closed subsets of $\{0, 1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$.
nodes.title: The Sidon ideal is $F_\sigma$

nodes.summary: Call a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ lacunary if it is infinite and the gaps $A(n + 1) - A(n)$ between consecutive elements tend to infinity, where $A(n)$ is the $n$-th element of $A$ in increasing order. Every set in the Sidon ideal is contained in a finite union of lacunary sets, that is, it lies in the ideal $\mathrm{Lac}$ generated by the lacunary sets.
nodes.title: The Sidon ideal is contained in the lacunary ideal

nodes.summary: The Sidon ideal $\mathrm{Si}$ is the ideal on $\mathbb{N}$ generated by the Sidon sets: it consists of all sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contained in a finite union of Sidon subsets of $\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Sidon ideal

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a property of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$, and consider the ideal generated by $P$, the family of all subsets of finite unions of sets with property $P$. If $A$ and $B$ lie in this ideal, then so does $A \cup B$.
nodes.title: Generated ideals are closed under unions

nodes.summary: The van der Waerden ideal $W$ consists of the sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ for which there is an $n > 0$ such that $A$ contains no arithmetic progression $a, a + r, \dots, a + (n - 1) r$ of $n$ terms with $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and $r > 0$.
nodes.title: Van der Waerden ideal
Combinatorics

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
